candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the bytes and, importantly, the entry names of the Node.js distribution archive that the framework downloads and extracts. The archive is obtained by DefaultFileDownloader from a URI derived from nodeDownloadRoot (NodeInstaller.install -> InstallData.downloadUrl/archive); NodeInstaller defaults to https://nodejs.org/dist/ but the root is configurable (NodeInstaller.setNodeDownloadRoot / FrontendTools constructor argument, documented for intranet mirrors) and DefaultFileDownloader also accepts a `file:` URI (line 82-83), so an attacker who can influence that configuration, serve a mirror, or intercept/replace the download supplies a malicious `.zip`. The `.zip` branch is selected on Windows (Platform.OS.WINDOWS -> getArchiveExtension() == "zip"; extract() dispatches on the archive file name suffix).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the TAR branch enforces containment (canonical path + startsWithPath, lines 133-148) but the ZIP branch does not; checked that extract() selects ZIP by file-name suffix and that Platform returns "zip" only on Windows; checked that the default download root is HTTPS nodejs.org (default exposure is therefore not remote out-of-the-box); checked DefaultFileDownloader for any archive-content validation (none, and it explicitly supports `file:` URIs); checked that ZipFile does not sanitize entry names; searched the rest of the repository for other ZIP extraction sites (only JarContentsManager, which reads trusted classpath jars). No tests are present in the snapshot to confirm intended behavior, and I could not compare against upstream history to verify whether this is a known fixed defect.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write with the privileges of the build/dev-mode process, outside the intended extraction directory: overwriting project files, configuration/startup scripts, or other locations writable by the process, which can corrupt the application or lead to code execution (e.g. planting/overwriting a script or file later executed by the build toolchain). The traversal also bypasses the AccessDeniedException check in prepDestination because the check is only on the (attacker-influenced) parent directory.
candidates.prerequisites: Windows host (ZIP extension) with a missing/invalid local Node installation so that NodeInstaller.install() runs during prepare-frontend/dev-mode/`build-frontend`; attacker ability to supply the downloaded archive (malicious mirror / configured download root / file: URI / download tampering). No authentication or victim interaction beyond triggering the build/dev bootstrap is needed once the archive source is controlled.
candidates.root_cause: DefaultArchiveExtractor.extractZipArchive() computes the output path as `new File(destinationDirectory + File.separator + entry.getName())` and immediately passes it to copyZipFileContents(), which opens a FileOutputStream on it. No normalization/canonical-path containment check is performed, so an entry name containing `..` segments (e.g. `..\..\some\file` on Windows or `../../some/file`) resolves outside destinationDirectory. The TAR branch of the same class (lines 133-148) does call startsWithPath(destPath.getCanonicalPath(), canonicalDestinationDirectory) and throws before copying, demonstrating the intended invariant that is missing for ZIP; the startsWithPath helper (lines 210-223) is never used by the ZIP path.
candidates.title: Zip Slip: ZIP entries extracted without path-containment check in DefaultArchiveExtractor (mirroring check exists only for TAR)
candidates.trace: FrontendTools.installNode(...) -> NodeInstaller.install() (line 197) -> installNode(InstallData) (line 245) -> downloadFileIfMissing(...) -> DefaultFileDownloader.download(...) (downloads or copies attacker-influenced archive) -> extractFile(archive, tmpDirectory) (lines 404-409) -> DefaultArchiveExtractor.extract(...) -> extractZipArchive(...) (line 81) -> destPath = new File(destinationDirectory + File.separator + entry.getName()) (lines 88-90) -> prepDestination(destPath, ...) creates parent directories (lines 183-197) -> copyZipFileContents(...) (lines 112-121) -> new FileOutputStream(destinationFile) writes entry bytes to the traversal path. A crafted entry name such as `..\..\..\..\<project-or-startup-path>\<file>` therefore escapes `installDirectory/node/tmp`.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Whether the default configuration alone is exploitable (without a controlled download root or download interception) is not established; the impact is limited to Windows ZIP extraction during build/dev bootstrap. It is also unverified whether the missing ZIP containment check is an upstream defect fixed later versus intended behavior inherited from the original frontend-maven-plugin code.
candidates.weakness_type: Path traversal in archive extraction (Zip Slip), CWE-22/CWE-29

coverage_summary: The assigned tree contains 1,891 main-source files (no test sources are present in the snapshot). I read or searched the flow-server entry points and request handlers (VaadinServlet, VaadinService, BootstrapHandler/BootstrapUtils, WebComponentBootstrapHandler/Provider, UidlRequestHandler/ServerRpcHandler and all RPC handlers, StreamRequestHandler/ResourceHandler/ReceiverHandler, StaticFileServer, WebJarServer, PWA/favicon/unsupported-browser handlers, PushHandler/BrowserLiveReload, ResponseWriter, DevModeHandler, DeploymentConfigurationFactory/DefaultDeploymentConfiguration), the frontend build/install tooling (FrontendTools, FrontendUtils, NodeInstaller, DefaultArchiveExtractor, DefaultFileDownloader, JarContentsManager, NodeTasks/AbstractUpdateImports), and performed targeted pattern searches across all modules for path handling, archive extraction, reflection, process execution, URL fetching, output/stream sinks and known hardening checks. Lighter, non-exhaustive checks were made of flow-client GWT sources, flow-data, flow-html-components, flow-dnd, flow-osgi, flow-maven-plugin and flow-migration.
limitations: Source-only review; no code was executed and no finding is runtime-confirmed.
The snapshot contains no test sources, so intended behavior and fix history could not be corroborated from tests.

A very large codebase was not read line-by-line; modules such as flow-data (Binder/converters), flow-client GWT internals, flow-osgi, flow-maven-plugin and flow-migration received only targeted searches.

The submitted candidate's exploitability depends on control of the Node archive source (configured download root, mirror, file: URI or download tampering) and on Windows ZIP extraction; default HTTPS download from nodejs.org limits exposure and this uncertainty is unresolved.
It could not be verified whether the missing ZIP containment check is a deliberate defect in this snapshot or pre-existing upstream behavior inherited from frontend-maven-plugin.

rejected_leads.lead: JarContentsManager.copyJarEntryTrimmingBasePath (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/frontend/JarContentsManager.java lines 303-323) writes `new File(outputDirectory, relativePath)` from raw jar entry names without containment validation.
rejected_leads.reason: Path is derived from jar entries of classpath dependencies. A malicious jar on the classpath is already trusted executable code in the same process, so no additional trust boundary is crossed compared with the downloaded-archive case, and the write happens at build time only.

rejected_leads.lead: WebComponentBootstrapHandler.getServiceUrl (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/communication/WebComponentBootstrapHandler.java lines 432-447) uses the request parameter `url` as the service base URL without host validation; only double quotes are rejected (checkURL, lines 395-404).
rejected_leads.reason: The value only flows into JSON app configuration and into `src` attributes through modifyPath/URI.create, which rejects characters needed for the obvious injection; exploiting it requires the attacker to already control the script URL on the embedding page. No concrete victim-side XSS/open-redirect was established from source.

rejected_leads.lead: FrontendUtils.getStatsFromExternalUrl (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/frontend/FrontendUtils.java lines 461-517) builds a server-side request URL from the client-controlled Host header when the external stats URL is relative.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires dev mode plus the non-default external-stats configuration; impact is blind SSRF in a development setup, much weaker than the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: VaadinServlet.handleContextOrServletRootWithoutSlash (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/VaadinServlet.java lines 314-343) sends a redirect built from request.getRequestURI()/getQueryString().
rejected_leads.reason: The location is derived from the request URI (same-origin by construction) and CR/LF are stripped from the query string; no cross-origin redirection control was demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: WebComponentUI.addAttributes (lines 361-371) and BootstrapUtils.createHeaderInjectionCall build JavaScript strings from theme attribute values.
rejected_leads.reason: Values originate from developer-defined theme classes/annotations, not from remote input, so this is not an attacker-controlled injection.
This is the documented developer API (developers are trusted with JavaScript execution); no remote attacker-controlled path sets attribute names.

summary: Reviewed the Vaadin Flow 2.6-SNAPSHOT snapshot source (1,891 main-source files; no test sources present in the assigned tree) with emphasis on remotely reachable code in flow-server (bootstrap, UIDL/RPC handlers, static/webjar serving, response writer/range handling, stream request/receive, PWA, push) and the frontend build/install tooling, plus lighter passes over flow-client, flow-data and the html-component modules. Most historical hardening is present (HandlerHelper.isPathUnsafe, Jsoup-cleaned RouteNotFoundError, MessageDigest.isEqual key comparison, CSRF token checks, ResponseWriter range limits), but one concrete missing containment check remains in the Node archive extraction path: the ZIP branch builds the destination path directly from the archive entry name and writes to it, while the TAR branch in the same class enforces a canonical-path containment check. I submit that as the single candidate; other suspicious areas were examined and rejected as weaker or non-exploitable from a real trust boundary.
